textbookBox.concept: Suppose a folded paper ends between two marks of the tenths scale. We split each tenth into 10 equal parts, giving hundredths.

beats.en: Suppose a folded paper ends between two marks of the tenths scale. We split each tenth into 10 equal parts, giving hundredths. A unit has 10 tenths, and each tenth has 10 hundredths, so a unit has 100 hundredths.
beats.speakEn: Suppose a folded paper ends between two marks of the tenths scale. We split each tenth into 10 equal parts, giving hundredths. A unit has 10 tenths, and each tenth has 10 hundredths, so a unit has 100 hundredths.

beats.en: Why do we split into 10 parts every time? Because in the Indian place value system each place is 10 times the one on its right. In 281, the 2 means hundreds, the 8 means tens and the 1 means ones.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 maths · A Peek Beyond the Point · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: We know that 1 cm = 10 mm, so 1 mm = 0.1 cm. A length of 5.6 cm is 5 cm and 6 mm, which is 56 mm. Also 1 m = 100 cm, so each cm is one hundredth of a metre. Therefore 15 cm = 0.15 m.

beats.en: Let us review the key takeaway from A Peek Beyond the Point: We know that 1 cm = 10 mm, so 1 mm = 0.1 cm. A length of 5.6 cm is 5 cm and 6 mm, which is 56 mm. Also 1 m = 100 cm, so each cm is one hundredth of a metre. Therefore 15 cm = 0.15 m.
beats.speakEn: Let us review the key takeaway from A Peek Beyond the Point: We know that 1 centimetres  equals  10 mm, so 1 mm  equals  0.1 centimetres. A length of 5.6 centimetres is 5 centimetres and 6 mm, which is 56 mm. Also 1 metres  equals  100 centimetres, so each cm is one hundredth of a metre. Therefore 15 centimetres  equals  0.15 metres.
